competences: The learner identifies facts about roles of district officials — part b.
The learner states responsibilities and qualities of leaders in the district.
languageCompetence: Pronounce, read and spell district, leader, officer, responsibility, appointment and service.
objectives: By the end of the lesson learners should identify the key points about roles of district officials — part b.
By the end of the lesson learners should answer five original district-leadership questions.
priorKnowledge: Learners have already studied district leaders, local councils and the services provided by appointed officials.
materials: Chart of district leaders and their duties
references: P4 Social Studies Notes for Terms 1–3

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher introduces roles of district officials — part b and asks "4. How do political leaders attain leadership powers?" to recall prior knowledge. They collect learners' responses and relate them to district leadership.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners recall earlier work on political and civic leaders, answer the starter question and name a district official.

steps.content: The district council plans development projects. The district chairperson supervises district officials. The RDC represents the president in the district. The district speaker chairs district council meetings. The DDHS supervises district health workers. The DEO supervises district education programmes. Agricultural officers advise crop farmers. Veterinary officers advise livestock farmers. District police officers maintain law and order. District water officers manage clean-water distribution. District councils help to settle disputes. Local leaders implement government policies.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the source-grounded points on remember, starting with "The district council plans development projects. The district chairperson supervises district officials." They check knowledge using the original question "7. Apart from the chairperson, mention any three other members on the LC I executive" and explain corrections.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners identify the relevant officials or leadership qualities, answer questions, and copy correct points into their books.

steps.content: 4. How do political leaders attain leadership powers? | 7. Apart from the chairperson, mention any three other members on the LC I executive | 13. Who is the president’s representative in the district? | 4. Give any four ways people in your district become leaders. | 3. Give any three roles played by cultural leaders in your community.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the supplied questions, beginning with "4. How do political leaders attain leadership powers?" and "7. Apart from the chairperson, mention any three other members on the LC I executive". They monitor learners' written answers, then mark and explain them using the reference notes.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners answer the questions individually, consult the notes and correct their written responses after marking.

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher checks understanding with "13. Who is the president’s representative in the district?" and "4. Give any four ways people in your district become leaders.". They review the relevant factual points and assign the final question for revision.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners give oral answers, state an important point and record the sourced homework question.

assessment: Check the original questions "4. How do political leaders attain leadership powers?", "7. Apart from the chairperson, mention any three other members on the LC I executive", and "13. Who is the president’s representative in the district?"; mark against the sourced facts.
homework: Complete the original question "3. Give any three roles played by cultural leaders in your community."
